Subject: Mini-window proration playbook and sample invoice lines

Tom —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As we head toward the 6-week pilot, you raised a few billing questions I wanted to put into a single, short note so procurement/finance can validate the mechanics before the kickoff. Main points we need to align on:

- Mini-window / heartbeat behavior: your app will open long-lived websockets and send periodic keep-alives. We treat each keep-alive as an active session heartbeat for the purposes of context retention.
- Per-token proration for short calls: how we round partial token usage for very short requests (sub-token-level in streaming scenarios).
- Context truncation and long-history treatment: how we bill if a conversation exceeds 32k and we keep a rolling window.
- Multi-region aggregation: whether traffic split across US/EU should be billed separately or aggregated under single committed capacity for the pilot.

Attached is a small sample of anonymized usage (pilot-usage-sample.csv) and the current pricing term sheet we agreed on. What I'm proposing for the pilot (so legal/procurement can quote a simple line on the PO):

1) Metering window: 30s heartbeat window. If a websocket has any activity in a 30s window, we count the window as active for context retention.
2) Token rounding: bill tokens to the nearest whole token using bankers rounding for aggregated windows (i.e., .5 rounds to nearest even integer) — but provide a per-call fallback where streaming partial tokens are accumulated across the minute and reconciled on invoice.
3) Context overflows: when conversation length > 32k, we bill the retained 32k window at the standard rate and annotate overflow tokens separately for audit.
4) Multi-region: for the pilot we will aggregate by account (one invoice) but show per-region breakout line items for visibility.

Can you confirm those four points are acceptable to Acme procurement? If not, flag which ones you need edits on and I’ll loop in Ben and Kimberly to cost the change.

Thanks,
Marissa

Ben/Kim —

Forwarding Acme's clarifying questions (below). I drafted a short playbook and a sample one-week reconciliation showing the three rounding approaches (ceiling, floor, bankers) attached as proposed-playbook-v1.docx. High level notes and answers:

- Burst behaviour: we bill per 30s window. So the pattern you described (3 msgs in 2s, idle 28s, another msg) equals a single 30s active window unless there is a socket close/open in between. If a socket is kept open, we count it once. If the client reconnects (socket close/open), that opens a new window.

- Rounding example (see playbook, table on p2): for low-volume accounts bankers rounding reduced invoice noise vs always ceilinging. Example week: 1,412.5 aggregated tokens -> bankers = 1,412, ceiling = 1,413, floor = 1,412. Over thousands of windows this evens out but for low-volume pilot accounts it can reduce apparent overage swings.

- Overflow tokens and pilot commitment: Recommendation — overflow tokens are billed as overage but capped at 25% of monthly committed tokens for the pilot. If overflow exceeds that, we notify and pause billing above cap until a threshold call with customer. This gives Acme predictability during pilot.

- Multi-region: keep one invoice with per-region line items. That avoids separate cross-region minimums while preserving visibility.

If you agree, I'll: 1) update proposed-playbook-v1.docx with the final cap numbers, 2) prepare a sample invoice (one page) and 3) draft the short FAQ for Acme Finance.

Marissa
